evidence_used: Object image showing a smooth, flat-sided white plastic bottle with a green cap
Gecko gripper embodiment requiring flat, parallel sidewalls and smooth nonporous surfaces for optimal dry adhesion
calculation_summary: Estimated object weight approximately 2.5 N based on visual scale; applying a gecko dry-adhesive benefit reduces the required normal lifting force significantly due to high surface compatibility, yielding an estimated stationary-finger normal force of 1.2 N.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: Object mass and center of mass are visually estimated without authoritative physical measurements
Sidewalls are assumed sufficiently flat and parallel to allow effective gecko pad contact
Visual approximation of surface texture carries inherent uncertainty
reasoning_trace: The visual evidence indicates a smooth, rigid plastic bottle with relatively flat sidewalls, which pairs exceptionally well with the rigid mushroom-tipped gecko-inspired dry-adhesive pads. Because the gecko embodiment achieves high directional adhesion on smooth, clean, nonporous plastic surfaces, a relatively low normal force is sufficient to generate the required holding capacity. Accounting for the estimated size and weight of the container, a normal force of 1.2 N provides a safe margin for lifting under zero-shot visual conditions.
